analysis: The experiment produced a small positive standalone delta (+0.000256 primary), but the paired 95% CI crossed zero (-0.000661 to +0.001224), so it does not establish that the strictly-prior affinity features reliably improve the incumbent. Portfolio benefit was even smaller (+0.000046) with a zero-crossing CI, and the challenger was not promoted. Directional slices are diagnostic only: gains appeared strongest for users with history >=65 and on tabs 4/6, but intermediate-history cohorts were negative, contradicting the expectation that benefit would broadly concentrate outside the <=16 slice. The positive effect in the <=16 slice also suggests the three bundled features may act through more than repeated-history personalization. Because author count, video count, and author share were added together, this result cannot identify which component helped or whether repeated-impression frequency and fatigue effects offset one another.
next_lesson: Treat the mechanism as weakly promising but unproven; next isolate the strictly-prior user-author affinity representation alone rather than adding all three features together.
